tldr: A revealed uniform simple regular network admits an explicit finite experiment whose worst-case direct-effect mean squared error is of order \(d/[n\log(d+1)]\), conditional on the entire graph, with graph probability tending to one throughout \(d\to\infty\), eventual \(d\le n^{2/3}\). Theorem \ref{thm:matched-rate} matches the published all-design, all-estimator lower bound on the original two separate endpoint second-moment balls. Local odds and capped marginal balancing deliver uniform vertex inclusion compatible with credited signed covariance control; a rational grid and posterior averaging yield an estimator using exactly \((G,Z,Y)\). The computation is finite and may be exponential. Polynomial implementation remains the separate acknowledged question \ref{oeq:efficient-attainment}; no normal approximation is asserted.
gap: Kandiros--Harshaw--S\"avje, Corollary 5.3, leaves a logarithmic gap between its all-design lower bound and constructive upper bound on typical regular networks.
fill: Local partition-function odds and capped marginal fitting supply a weighted independent-set law compatible with a credited Poincar\'{e} inequality. A finite rational grid and posterior averaging convert the law into an experiment and estimator on the original observation record.
